title: Tempo field controls
contract: The Control Bar tempo field adjusts Set playback tempo through coarse BPM and fine hundredths-of-BPM controls, which can be key/MIDI mapped separately. This supplies named direct edit/control roles only; numeric storage, ranges, interpolation and mapping protocol retain existing owners.

title: Tap Tempo inputs
contract: Tap Tempo accepts mouse clicks, a key assigned through Key Map Mode, or a MIDI note/controller assigned through MIDI Map Mode. Tap estimation, dispatch latency and accuracy remain ungraded.

title: Tap-start option
contract: Start Playback with Tap Tempo in Record, Warp & Launch Settings enables tap-triggered playback; the source describes four taps in 4/4. It also describes tap-start automatically synchronizing connected Link-app playback positions within the current phrase. This is a qualitative source role, with no estimator, interval tolerance, other-meter count, phase/phrase arithmetic, Link alignment or scheduling oracle.

title: Phase Nudge controls
contract: Phase Nudge Up/Down can temporarily speed or slow playback and can be key/MIDI mapped. Rate, duration, recovery curve, phase and external synchronization are unknown.

title: Audio clip Lead and Follow
contract: Warped audio clips are documented as followers by default; Arrangement clips can select Lead through Audio Utilities Lead/Follow. This is documentary context, not an exact-target constructor default or Session eligibility rule.

title: Leader role and disabled tempo field
contract: For an active tempo leader, clip Warp Markers determine Set tempo and the Control Bar tempo field is deactivated. The source describes leader playback as if unwarped; no time-map, DSP or sample equality follows.

title: Leader-generated automation presentation
contract: Tempo automation tracking leader/Set tempo changes appears in Main and is not editable; rearranging leader clips moves the corresponding automation. Exact points, ownership boundaries and scheduling remain unknown.

title: Unfollow Tempo Automation
contract: Unfollow Tempo Automation in the tempo field context menu makes all leader clips followers and makes the Main tempo automation editable. Envelope point identity, numerical values and Undo are unknown.

title: External sync toggle eligibility
contract: With EXT enabled, the Lead/Follow toggle is deactivated. Accepted external source, protocol, activation timing and fallback remain unknown.

title: Leader versus audio Tempo Follower
contract: Clip-leader tempo automation is documented to override tempo from an audio input synchronized through Tempo Follower. This does not establish all tempo-source precedence or real-time alignment.

title: Short-sample load policy controls
contract: Record, Warp & Launch Settings offers Loop/Warp Short Samples: Unwarped One Shot, Warped One Shot, Warped Loop and Auto. The first is unwarped; the second warped using Default Warp Mode without looping; the third warped/looped. Auto chooses a policy and is documented as selected by default. Classification threshold and Auto choice remain unknown.

title: Long-sample load policy
contract: Auto-Warp Long Samples is documented enabled by default. Enabled requests automatic warping on load; disabled loads long samples unwarped. The source claims a first-beat-per-bar marker policy, without establishing analysis or exact marker results for any supplied sample.

title: Default Warp Mode preference
contract: Default Warp Mode selects the mode applied when samples are warped; this chapter describes Beats as the initial default. This documentary default does not settle missing-field load behavior, preference precedence or exact-target factory state.

title: Insert an interactive Warp Marker
contract: In the Sample Editor upper half, double-click adds a Warp Marker; Ctrl+I (Windows)/Cmd+I (macOS) places one at the insert marker. Selection-driven insertion has its separate documented context below. Numeric marker validation, identity and scripting limits are not imported.

title: Move interactive markers
contract: Warp Markers can be dragged or moved with arrow keys to change their timeline placement. Step size, snapping, bounds, rounding and audio output are unknown here.

title: Shift waveform under a marker
contract: With a Warp Marker selected, Shift-drag moves the waveform beneath the marker to adjust the audio starting point under it. Exact coordinate transformation and collateral marker changes are unknown.

title: Delete interactive Warp Markers
contract: Double-click deletes a Warp Marker; selecting its corresponding time and pressing Backspace (Windows)/Delete (macOS) is another documented route. Last/protected markers, deduplication and exact resulting list remain unknown.

title: Transient presentation and editing
contract: Detected transients appear as small gray markers. Create menu and Ctrl+Shift+I (Windows)/Cmd+Shift+I (macOS) create transients; Ctrl+Shift+Backspace (Windows)/Cmd+Shift+Delete (macOS) deletes them. Detection output and numerical positions remain unknown.

title: Reset manually created transients
contract: Sample Editor Reset Transients removes all manually created transients. The source does not establish restoration of moved/deleted automatically detected transients or exact redetection results.

title: Selection-based Warp Marker insertion
contract: Insert Warp Markers in Create or Ctrl+I (Windows)/Cmd+I (macOS) creates markers for selected-area transients. For a selected area containing no transients, the source describes markers at selection start and end. Numerical endpoint, count/deduplication and detector outcomes remain unknown.

title: Pseudo-marker conversion
contract: Hovering a transient shows a gray pseudo-Warp Marker; the source contrasts this with a yellow real Warp Marker. Double-click or drag converts the pseudo-marker to a real Warp Marker. Literal color names supply no palette/RGB/image oracle. The source says clip tempo changes if no Warp Markers follow the new one, without a numerical tempo oracle.

title: Pseudo-marker adjacent anchors
contract: Ctrl (Windows)/Cmd (macOS) while creating a real marker from a pseudo-marker also creates Warp Markers at adjacent transients. First/last transient, duplicates and exact resulting lists remain unknown.

title: Move transient via pseudo-marker
contract: Shift-dragging a pseudo-marker moves the transient to a new Sample Editor location. This is distinct from moving waveform under a selected real Warp Marker.

title: Saved markers and Auto-Warp
contract: A sample saved with Warp Markers is unaffected by ordinary Auto-Warp; manual Warp From context commands remain available. Saving default clip settings and their media scope remain with the media owner. Exact identity/ASD precedence and corruption outcomes remain unknown.

title: Clip BPM and Arrangement edge adjustment
contract: Audio Utilities BPM shows estimated sample tempo, permits direct known-BPM input and Shift-drag fine adjustment. Shift-drag from an Arrangement clip edge stretches or compresses its tempo. Accepted range, increment, anchors and timing arithmetic are unknown.

title: Double and halve clip tempo
contract: The clip tempo ×2 and ÷2 buttons double or halve estimated tempo for correction. Limits, repeated-operation rounding and resulting marker/sample mapping remain unknown.

title: Set 1.1.1 Here contexts
contract: For an uneven short-loop example, moving the insert marker to the downbeat and Set 1.1.1 Here places a Warp Marker there; in the long-sample correction example the command moves the start marker to that downbeat. Preserve these source contexts without asserting a complete region/marker transform.

title: Same-length multi-clip marker editing
contract: For multiple clips of the same length, adding or adjusting Warp Markers in one applies the changes to all selected clips. Length equality definition, mixed Warp/region states, deletion and unequal-length behavior remain unknown.

title: Warp Sample as command
contract: For a seamlessly edited loop, Warp Sample as in the Sample Editor context menu can be invoked to adjust Auto-Warp results and displays a suggested loop length fitting Set tempo. This is a public command/suggestion role only; the suggested value, algorithm, accepted bounds, generated markers and audio results remain ungraded.

title: Warp Selection as command
contract: Warp Selection as operates on selected sample time; the source describes assumed loop length, loop start/end markers and warping to fill the loop. Algorithm choice, exact markers, bounds and audio are ungraded.

title: Move multiple Warp Markers
contract: Ctrl (Windows)/Cmd (macOS) selects multiple Warp Markers for moving together. Anchor, spacing, snapping, coordinate and refusal laws remain unknown.

title: Warp From Here scope
contract: Warp From Here context commands reset markers to the right of the chosen grid division/marker while leaving left-side markers unchanged. The basic command requests Auto-Warp to the right and adds a marker at the specified grid point if none is selected. Exact generated list and selected-point ownership remain unknown.

title: Warp From Here Start At baseline
contract: Warp From Here (Start At …) uses Set tempo as the Auto-Warp baseline. The described preparation turns Warp off, taps the source tempo, re-enables Warp and invokes the command. Estimation and generated marker outcomes remain unknown.

title: Warp From Here Straight
contract: Warp From Here (Straight) is intended for material without tempo variation; the source describes one starting marker based on estimated original BPM. This is a source claim, not a graded automatic marker count or position for unprovided media.

title: Warp BPM From Here
contract: Warp … BPM From Here assumes source tempo equals Set tempo and describes a single starting marker. Known BPM may be entered in Control Bar before invoking it; exact resulting map and boundary handling remain unknown.

title: Quantize command focus
contract: With Sample Editor focused, Edit Quantize or Ctrl+U (Windows)/Cmd+U (macOS) uses current Quantize settings. Clip View owns the Quantize panel availability and grid/Amount controls.

title: Audio quantization role
contract: The source describes moving a nearest transient to a closest grid line; current or specific/triplet grid and Amount affect Warp Marker movement. Selection, ties, Amount equation, marker generation and exact output remain unknown. Groove application/commit remains groove-owned.

title: Beats Preserve control
contract: Beats mode exposes Preserve with Transients or grid divisions to choose segment divisions. Actual segmentation, transient preservation, grains, crossfades, values and output quality are ungraded; stored enums/settings remain Warp-marker-owned.

title: Beats Transient Loop modes
contract: Transient Loop Mode offers Loop Off, Loop Forward and Loop Back-and-Forth. The source describes segment stop/silence, forward looping and alternating direction respectively; zero-crossing choice, endpoints, loops and delivered audio remain unknown.

title: Transient Envelope role
contract: Transient Envelope controls segment fades; the source describes no fade at 100 and quicker decay at 0. No numeric gain envelope, time constant, normalization, detector or click-quality criterion follows. Existing stored range/default uncertainty remains unchanged.

title: Tones Grain Size role
contract: Tones exposes Grain Size for approximate average grain size, described as affected by pitch clarity. Suggested material and grain size are guidance, not a pitch detector, DSP, noise or quality guarantee.

title: Texture controls
contract: Texture exposes Grain Size and Fluctuation; the former is described independently of tonal characteristics, the latter as increasing processing randomness. No RNG, seed, distribution, correlation, grain process or monotonic statistical oracle is established.

title: Re-Pitch control and signal role
contract: Re-Pitch changes playback rate and pitch with tempo; its sample transposition controls are deactivated. The doubled-rate/octave source example is descriptive, not a new rate-conversion or sample-accuracy contract.

title: Complex Pro Formants and Envelope
contract: Complex Pro exposes Formants and Envelope. The source describes formant preservation at 100% with transposition and no Formants effect without transposition; Envelope changes tonal character. Exact response, defaults/ranges and byte values retain existing storage owner or remain unknown; no quality/CPU guarantee is inferred.

title: Detection and automatically generated markers
contract: Short/long classification, initial BPM/markers, downbeat accuracy, transient detection and exact output of every Auto-Warp/Warp From/Selection/Sample command require evidence. Short-loop and odd-loop examples do not provide universal estimators or correct marker positions.

title: Warp audio and randomness
contract: Per-mode audio/pitch/time behavior, Formants/Envelope/Transient settings, zero-crossing/grain behavior, resampling, tail/phase continuity, determinism and comparison tolerances remain unknown. Manual material/quality recommendations and internal explanations are not required implementation mechanisms.

title: Interactive limits and quantization boundaries
contract: Interactive marker/region limits, protected/shadow edits, duplicate/order/selection transforms, near/equal boundaries, unequal multi-clips, quantization ties and Amount rounding remain unknown. Existing scripting limits do not establish interactive behavior.

title: Tempo and transport interactions
contract: Tap estimation/start schedule, nudge curves, leader handoffs and tempo/automation/scene/external-source precedence, live edit dispatch and clip-update timing remain unknown beyond documented controls. The existing video owner retains its documented active-leader selection context.

title: State and lifecycle
contract: Marker/default/analysis interactions on save/reopen/migration, undo/redo, cancel, automation during edits, source/device loss, rate/engine changes, errors and teardown have no complete oracle. Existing finite storage/reader/ASD contracts retain their scope.

title: Import source differences
contract: This chapter first-import readiness and Import Audio File format/destination text is retained context, not a complete codec or readiness law. Its all-first-import wording versus media owner long-analysis wording, accepted AAC/Ogg variants, platform scope and destination interactions require separate reconciliation.
